references.text: The same song celebrates God's majesty and victory over the enemies
Describes God's majesty (גאון) riding on the heavens to help His people
God's wrath (חרון) against the enemies as resistance against His people
Fire that consumes enemies like straw (קש), using the same imagery for God's judgment
Straw (קש) consumed by fire as a symbol of God's judgment on the wicked
Straw burning in the fire as an image of God's judgment
Enemies are consumed like dry straw, using the same imagery for God's judgment
The proud become like straw that burns up on the Lord's day
God's burning wrath that will consume the adversaries
God's wrath striking the nations, fulfilling God's victory over the enemies
Both verses confirm that hostility toward God leads to inevitable destruction, either through active punishment or by being wiped out when one keeps away.
Psalm 21:10 expands on the image of God's wrath from Exodus 15:7 by using the metaphor of a burning furnace that swallows up the enemies.
Isaiah 41:11 confirms the result of the action described in Exodus 15:7: those who rise against God become nothing.
Psalm 68:3 uses similar metaphors (smoke/wax) as Exodus 15:7 (straw) to illustrate the enemy's complete powerlessness before God's wrath.
Deuteronomy 33:11 asks that God should crush those who rise against Him, directly repeating and expanding on the action described in Exodus 15:7.
Deuteronomy 7:24 expands on the consequence of Exodus 15:7 by promising that no enemy will be able to stand against God's people until they are completely destroyed.
Micah 5:8 confirms and repeats the theme of God's hand being raised to wipe out all enemies, just as in Exodus 15:7.
